hook: One water molecule speeds up iodide's reaction with ozone about 23-fold.

readout.label: Rate boost from one attached water molecule

summary: Sea-surface iodide destroys ozone, and a single attached water molecule makes that reaction about 23 times faster. Mass spectrometry of isolated ions, backed by quantum calculations, shows water helps through hydrogen bonding. The measurements are gas-phase ion experiments, so the extrapolation to real seawater and polar air rests on modeling.
title: A Single Water Molecule Drives a 20-Fold Acceleration in the Gas-Phase Reaction of Iodide with Ozone
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
